facts.text: Field recordings support camera and lidar replay and novel-view simulation close to the recorded path, provided the recordings were made with reconstruction in mind.
facts.quote: Recordings work for camera and lidar replay and for novel-view simulation close to the recorded path, provided they were recorded with reconstruction in mind.

facts.text: Field recordings do not support radar or ultrasonic re-simulation, large viewpoint or height changes, or adding weather.
facts.quote: They do not work for radar or ultrasonic re-simulation, for large viewpoint or height changes, or for adding weather

facts.text: A one-pass reconstruction can look excellent but become inaccurate as soon as a sensor moves substantially away from the recording trajectory.
facts.quote: a one-pass reconstruction can look excellent while becoming inaccurate as soon as a sensor moves substantially from the recording trajectory.

facts.text: Structure from motion and multi-view stereo can convert a camera-only log into poses, dense points and a textured mesh.
facts.quote: A camera-only log can be converted by structure from motion and multi-view stereo into poses, dense points and a textured mesh.

facts.text: Combining camera recordings with lidar makes metric geometry easier to constrain.
facts.quote: Camera plus lidar makes metric geometry easier to constrain.

facts.text: Lidar combined with IMU or GNSS, or lidar-inertial SLAM, produces a directly mapped point cloud.
facts.quote: Lidar plus IMU or GNSS, or lidar-inertial SLAM, gives a directly mapped point cloud.

facts.text: Geometry outputs reconstructed from field recordings can be converted into explicit terrain and objects.
facts.quote: These outputs convert to explicit terrain and objects.

facts.text: Logs and their poses can train a NeRF or 3DGS scene representation as an alternative to explicit geometry conversion.
facts.quote: Alternatively, logs and their poses train a NeRF or 3DGS representation

facts.text: Neural lidar models such as GS-LiDAR (ICLR 2025) learn ray-drop and intensity from recordings and reproduce the recorded sensor rather than a new sensor type.
facts.quote: neural lidar models learn ray-drop and intensity from the recordings (GS-LiDAR, ICLR 2025), so they reproduce the recorded sensor rather than a new sensor type

facts.text: No validated evidence supports re-simulating a different sensor type from recordings, such as radar from camera-only logs.
facts.quote: re-simulating a different sensor, for example radar from camera-only logs, has no validated evidence.

facts.text: Replay-quality field recordings provide original video, sensor streams and machine motion.
facts.quote: Replay | Original video and sensor streams and machine motion

facts.text: Replay cannot change machine path, sensor position, actors or site state.
facts.quote: Cannot change machine path, sensor position, actors or site state

facts.text: Novel-view or perception simulation provides reconstructed geometry or a neural scene and synthetic camera and lidar outputs from nearby new viewpoints.
facts.quote: Reconstructed geometry or neural scene; synthetic camera and lidar from nearby new viewpoints

facts.text: Novel-view or perception simulation may have incomplete extrapolation accuracy, object editability and sensor-material fidelity.
facts.quote: Extrapolation accuracy, object editability and sensor-material fidelity may be incomplete

facts.text: A closed-loop braking environment includes explicit geometry, terrain, objects, a calibrated sensor model, dynamic agents and machine dynamics.
facts.quote: Closed-loop braking environment | Explicit geometry, terrain, objects, calibrated sensor model, dynamic agents, machine dynamics

facts.text: Creating a closed-loop braking environment from recordings requires substantial conversion and calibration beyond ordinary reconstruction.
facts.quote: Substantial conversion and calibration beyond ordinary reconstruction

facts.text: XLD, a June 2024 preprint with a 2025 v3 using synthetic CARLA data, reported 3DGS PSNR of 30.87, 23.26, 22.01 and 19.17 dB at lateral shifts of 0, 1, 2 and 4 m respectively.
facts.quote: XLD (June 2024, v3 2025, preprint, synthetic CARLA) | 0, 1, 2, 4 m lateral | 3DGS: 30.87, 23.26, 22.01, 19.17 dB PSNR

facts.text: In the XLD synthetic CARLA benchmark, EmerNeRF had the best PSNR at a 4 m lateral shift, at 24.80 dB.
facts.quote: best at 4 m: EmerNeRF 24.80 dB [6]

facts.text: Para-Lane (3DV 2025), using real data, reported 3DGS PSNR of 22.99, 17.05 and 16.26 dB for the same, adjacent and second-adjacent lanes respectively.
facts.quote: Para-Lane (3DV 2025, real) | same, adjacent, second-adjacent lane | 3DGS: 22.99, 17.05, 16.26 dB

facts.text: In Para-Lane (3DV 2025), the best method, Scaffold-GS, reported PSNR of 22.96, 17.59 and 17.09 dB for the same, adjacent and second-adjacent lanes respectively.
facts.quote: same, adjacent, second-adjacent lane | 3DGS: 22.99, 17.05, 16.26 dB; best (Scaffold-GS) 22.96, 17.59, 17.09 dB [5]

facts.text: EUVS (ICCV 2025), using real data, reported average PSNR reductions of 24.6% for translation, 25.6% for rotation and 30.6% for both.
facts.quote: EUVS (ICCV 2025, real) | translation / rotation / both | average PSNR minus 24.6% / minus 25.6% / minus 30.6%

facts.text: EUVS (ICCV 2025), using real data, reported LPIPS increases of up to 70% under viewpoint changes.
facts.quote: LPIPS up to plus 70% [7]

facts.text: MV², an August 2026 preprint using real data, reported a 3DGS PSNR decrease from 24.22 to 16.78 dB when changing from car to scooter viewpoints.
facts.quote: MV² (August 2026, preprint, real) | car to scooter; drone to car | 3DGS 24.22 to 16.78 dB

facts.text: MV², an August 2026 preprint using real data, reported drone-trained 3DGS PSNR decreasing from 29.13 to 10.36 dB when changing from drone to car viewpoints.
facts.quote: drone-trained 3DGS 29.13 to 10.36 dB [8]

facts.text: LiDAR-EVS, a March 2026 preprint, claims Chamfer distances 48.6% and 47.2% lower than SplatAD for lidar at a 3 m lateral shift; absolute values were not extracted.
facts.quote: LiDAR-EVS (March 2026, preprint) | 3 m lateral, lidar | Chamfer distance 48.6% and 47.2% lower than SplatAD (authors' claim; absolute values not extracted) [17]

facts.text: LiDAR-EVS describes single-traversal 3DGS as suffering from severe overfitting and poor generalisation on novel ego paths.
facts.quote: LiDAR-EVS describes single-traversal 3DGS as suffering from severe overfitting and poor generalisation on novel ego paths

facts.text: VEGS (July 2024) addresses the problem of severe overfitting and poor generalisation of single-traversal 3DGS on novel ego paths.
facts.quote: severe overfitting and poor generalisation on novel ego paths; VEGS (July 2024) exists for the same reason.

facts.text: LiDAR-EVS and VEGS attempt to remedy novel-path reconstruction problems but do not demonstrate that those problems have disappeared.
facts.quote: These papers try to remedy the problem; they are not evidence that it has disappeared.

facts.text: Diffusion repair methods help but do not close the novel-view gap: for Para-Lane two-lane shifts, the best reported PSNR is 19.47 dB with ViewMorpher3D / SetDiff (January 2026), versus about 23 dB on the recorded path.
facts.quote: on Para-Lane two-lane shifts the best reported score is 19.47 dB PSNR (ViewMorpher3D / SetDiff, January 2026) against about 23 dB on the recorded path.

facts.text: Viewpoint-height degradation is directly relevant to large machines whose sensors sit well above car height.
facts.quote: The height result is directly relevant to large machines whose sensors sit well above car height

facts.text: A car-to-truck height study was not found.
facts.quote: a car-to-truck height study was not found.

facts.text: Field recordings intended for reconstruction need hardware-synchronised timestamps and retained calibration, including camera intrinsics, all sensor-to-machine extrinsics and accurate timing.
facts.quote: Hardware-synchronised timestamps and retained calibration: camera intrinsics, all sensor-to-machine extrinsics and accurate timing.

facts.text: Para-Lane used 10 Hz cameras with 1920 by 1080 resolution and three 32-channel lidars, with sensor data fused after motion compensation.
facts.quote: Para-Lane used 10 Hz 1920 by 1080 cameras and three 32-channel lidars, fused after motion compensation.

facts.text: For rolling or scanning sensors, per-frame timestamps may be insufficient if the machine moves significantly during a scan.
facts.quote: For rolling or scanning sensors, per-frame timestamps may not suffice if the machine moves significantly during a scan.
